question: Who was the mastermind behind the Arabari Project of West Bengal, which started in 1972?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. AK Banerjee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dr. AK Banerjee** was the mastermind behind the Arabari Project in West Bengal, which started in 1972.
 
• The Arabari Project aimed at involving the local community in forest management and conservation.
 
• It was one of the pioneering projects in India that utilized the concept of **Joint Forest Management (JFM)**.
 
• Under Dr. Banerjee's leadership, the project successfully regenerated degraded forests and improved the livelihoods of local communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arabari Project**

 
 
• The Arabari Project was initiated in the Midnapore district of West Bengal, covering around 1,272 hectares of forest land.
 
• The project sought to involve local villagers in forest protection, in return for a share of the benefits derived from the forest resources.
 
• This approach marked the beginning of Joint Forest Management (JFM) in India.
 
 
 
• **Joint Forest Management (JFM)**
 
 
• JFM is a concept where the local communities are involved in the management and conservation of forests.
 
• It aims to enhance forest cover and improve the socio-economic conditions of the local communities.
 
• The JFM approach has been recognized as a successful model for forest management in various parts of India.
 
 
 
• **Dr. AK Banerjee**
 
 
• Dr. AK Banerjee was a visionary forest officer who believed in the participation of local communities in forest conservation.
 
• His work in the Arabari Project is considered a landmark in the history of forest management in India.
 
• He demonstrated that sustainable forest management is possible through community involvement and benefit-sharing mechanisms.
